stances.claim: The Supreme Court should not wait years (as it did with Ampatuan) to issue special guidelines -- it should act now to hasten the pork cases.

ONE special division (not two) is the better option, with justices cleared of all other dockets -- modeled on the Ampatuan-massacre framework where PJ Solis-Reyes was given assisting judges and five SC guidelines.
stances.rhetorical_move: one-not-two prescriptive refinement of OOO proposal

stances.claim: Multiple divisions risk differing rulings, repeated testimonies, multiple legal teams, and unnecessary delays -- already demonstrated by the divergent probable-cause treatment (First Division issued warrants immediately; Third and Fifth held hearings first).
Without innovative and creative solutions, the pork cases will drag on for decades, prejudicing both the innocent (who may be detained pending trial) and the public interest.

notable_anecdotes: The divergent probable-cause treatment across divisions -- First Division simply adjudged probable cause and issued warrants on Revilla et al., while Third and Fifth Divisions opted to hold hearings first -- used as live, contemporaneous proof that multi-division raffle produces inconsistent procedure on the very same legal question.

The June 16 Inquirer editorial demolishing the myth that special divisions are created to nail down the accused -- the Special Division convicted Estrada but acquitted Jinggoy Estrada and Edward Serapio -- deployed to neutralize the political objection to creating a special division.

The Ampatuan-massacre framework explicitly invoked as the model: emptied docket of PJ Jocelyn Solis-Reyes, assisting judges, five special guidelines -- with the lament that the SC waited four years to act, which the Court should not repeat with pork.

Drilon bill triple-reform mention -- more SBN slots, single-justice trials (instead of three), and moving minor graft cases to regular courts -- the only legislative-side proposal Panganiban endorses in the column.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban argues that the SC's decision to let the Sandiganbayan raffle the pork barrel cases to its different divisions -- despite the OOO's request for two special divisions -- signals that the cases will get no special treatment for now, but warns that without innovative procedural acceleration the cases will take more than a decade to resolve. He prefers ONE special division (not two), with justices cleared of all other dockets on the Ampatuan-massacre template (PJ Solis-Reyes, assisting judges, five SC special guidelines from his Jan 12 2014 column), and points to the divergent probable-cause treatment -- First Division issuing warrants immediately on Revilla et al. while Third and Fifth Divisions held hearings first -- as live evidence that multi-division raffle produces inconsistent procedure on the same legal question. He inventories the docket: 45 cases filed (1 plunder + 16 graft per senator cluster against Revilla, Cambe, Napoles, Lim, De Asis and others), each accused with at least one lawyer filing petitions and motions, truckloads of documents to be authenticated. He notes the SBN's internal rules already permit a special division recommendation (as belatedly done in the Estrada trial), joint trials, or consolidation, and demolishes the June 16 Inquirer editorial's debunking of the myth that special divisions exist to nail down the accused -- the Estrada Special Division convicted the President but acquitted Jinggoy and Edward Serapio. He endorses Drilon's bill expanding SBN slots, authorizing single-justice trials, and moving minor graft cases to regular courts, and closes with the warning that unless creative solutions are deployed, the cases will drag on for decades to the prejudice of innocent and public interest alike -- citing his June 1 transcendental-importance rallying cry Yes, the Supreme Court can!
